newsitem.title: USA: BPA drops Tues firm peak power prices by 75cts/MWh.
newsitem.headline: BPA drops Tues firm peak power prices by 75cts/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) lowered prices for firm power during peak demand hours on Tuesday by 75 cents per megawatt hour (MWh), the agency said Monday.
BPA still offered up to 300 megawatts of firm peak power, but lowered prices to $14.00 per MWh for Northwest sales and $15.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
Prices for non-firm power during shoulder hours on Tuesday (0600, 1100-1700 and 2100-2200 PST) were unchanged at $12.00 per MWh for Northwest sales and $13.00 for COB.
BPA continued to refrain from offering non-firm power during morning and evening peaks or any displacement power.
Prices for firm and non-firm power during off-peak hours on Tuesday were unchanged at $9.00 per MWh for all deliveries.
